title: Buyers vs Sellers
hook: Price isn't moving because your candle turned green. The candle turned green because price moved.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain what buyer and seller aggression actually means — without treating any single candle as the whole story.

blocks.heading: What buyers and sellers actually do

beats.heading: Buyers showing aggression
beats.body: Participants willing to transact at increasingly higher available prices — that's what pushes price up.

beats.heading: Sellers showing aggression
beats.body: Participants willing to transact at increasingly lower available prices — that's what pushes price down.

beats.heading: One candle isn't the whole story
beats.body: One green candle does NOT establish a bullish market. One red candle does NOT establish a bearish market. This prepares you for reading structure later.

blocks.heading: Find where control changed
blocks.prompt: This price path steps higher with a couple of small pullbacks, then something changes. Tap the point where sellers actually took control.

points.feedback: That's a small pullback inside an uptrend that's still holding — not a real change of control.
Exactly. That's the point where price actually closed lower and broke the pattern — a real shift, not just a wick.
Another shallow pullback — buyers were still winning through this point.

blocks.heading: Is she right?
blocks.scenario: Price prints a small green candle, then a large green candle, then a small red candle. A trader says the red candle means sellers now control the entire market.

options.label: No — one candle without context doesn't tell us the larger structural story
options.feedback: Right. We need more than one candle to know whether the bigger story actually changed.

options.label: Yes — any red candle after green ones means sellers have taken over
options.feedback: One candle isn't enough evidence to declare a full change of control.

blocks.quote: Stop asking what one candle means by itself. Eventually, we'll learn to ask what that candle is doing within structure.

questions.question: Price has been moving higher for several hours. A single bearish candle forms. Which conclusion is most justified from that information alone?
options: We need more context before determining whether the larger story changed
questions.why: One candle isn't enough to declare a reversal — you need the larger structural story.

questions.question: A string of strong green closes with small pullbacks usually means:
questions.why: Repeated strong closes with shallow pullbacks is buyers repeatedly winning the disagreement.

takeaways: Buyer aggression pushes price up; seller aggression pushes price down.
One candle doesn't establish a trend or a reversal on its own.
Later, you'll learn to read what a candle is doing within structure — not just by itself.
remember: Don't ask what one candle means by itself.
